place.name: 예루살렘1
place.description:
Jerusalem, called the “great city” and the capital of the kingdom of [Judah|judah], is the place from which the record opens. {Lehi|lehi1} had dwelt there all his days when, in the first year of the reign of {Zedekiah|zedekiah1} king of [Judah|judah] (about 600 BC), many prophets came warning the people that they must repent or the city would be destroyed. {Lehi|lehi1} was among them, and he was commanded by {God|god} to take his family and flee (1 Nephi 1:4).

{Lehi|lehi1}’s departure became the record’s timeline marker: six hundred years from the time he left Jerusalem, {the Lord|jesus-christ} would raise up a {Messiah|jesus-christ}, a {Savior|jesus-christ} of the world, among {the Jews|jews} (1 Nephi 10:4). In vision, {Nephi|nephi1} saw the great city of Jerusalem and other cities, including [Nazareth|nazareth], where he beheld the virgin who would be the mother of {the Son of God|jesus-christ} (1 Nephi 11:13). {Nephi|nephi1} wrote of his own anguish of spirit for those who remained at Jerusalem, whom {the Lord|jesus-christ} had shown him would otherwise have perished (1 Nephi 19:20).

{Lehi|lehi1} told his sons he had seen a vision in which he knew Jerusalem was destroyed, and that had they stayed they too would have died (2 Nephi 1:4). {Nephi|nephi1} recorded the prophecy that those at Jerusalem would crucify {the God of Israel|jesus-christ} and be scourged by all people for it (1 Nephi 19:13), and that though the people were carried away, they would return and again possess the land of Jerusalem, their land of inheritance (2 Nephi 25:11).

The record also preserves an eschatological distinction about Jerusalem’s ultimate fate. {Moroni|moroni2}, abridging the vision of {Ether|ether}, records that the Jerusalem from which {Lehi|lehi1} came would, after its destruction, be built up again as a holy city of {the Lord|jesus-christ} — yet it could not be the New Jerusalem, for it was already ancient; a separate New Jerusalem would be built on the American continent for the remnant of the seed of {Joseph|joseph1} (Ether 13:5–6).

place.info: 제이라헤믈라 인근 지역에 대한 일반적인 언급
place.description:
The Land of Zarahemla lay in the northern part of the land southward, along the [river Sidon|sidon-river], which ran by the land of Zarahemla (Alma 2:15). It was settled by the {Mulekites|mulekites}, who left [Jerusalem|jerusalem-1] about the time {Zedekiah|zedekiah1}, king of [Judah|judah], was carried captive to [Babylon|babylon] in the sixth century B.C. and crossed the great waters to their landing place (Omni 1:15, Alma 22:29-31). Around 200 B.C. {Mosiah1|mosiah1}, warned to flee [the land of Nephi|land-of-nephi], led his people through the wilderness and found the {people of Zarahemla|zarahemla-brethren}, named for their leader {Zarahemla|zarahemla}. The two peoples united and made {Mosiah|mosiah1} their king (Omni 1:12-19).

The temple at Zarahemla was the site of King {Benjamin|benjamin}’s great covenant convocation, in which the assembled multitude pitched their tents round about the temple, each with its door facing toward the temple, and {Benjamin|benjamin} preached from a tower because the crowd was too great to fit within the temple walls (Mosiah 1:18; 2:5-7). At the close of that assembly the people entered a covenant and were given a new name, being called “the children of Christ, his sons, and his daughters” (Mosiah 5:7).

Under king {Mosiah|mosiah2}’s reign {Alma1|alma1} established seven churches throughout the land of Zarahemla (Mosiah 25:15-23), and at the close of the monarchy {Alma2|alma2} became the first chief judge over the reign of judges seated there (Mosiah 29:42). {Samuel the Lamanite|samuel} came into the land of Zarahemla and preached repentance to its people (Hel. 13–16). The land changed hands repeatedly in war: dissenters under {Pachus|pachus} seized the city, set up a king, and allied with the {Lamanites|lamanites} until {Moroni|moroni1} and {Pahoran|pahoran1} retook it and {Pachus|pachus} was slain (Alma 61-62:9); the Lamanite-allied {Coriantumr|coriantumr3} stormed and took the city before {Moronihah|moronihah1} recovered it (Hel. 1:14-33); and dissenters with a Lamanite army held the land until {Moronihah|moronihah1} regained half of it (Hel. 4:1-17).

The [city of Zarahemla|zarahemla] took fire and its inhabitants were burned at the death of {Jesus Christ|jesus-christ} (3 Ne. 8:8, 24; 9:3). It was built again in the first century A.D. and was covered with buildings and people as numerous as the sand of the sea when {Mormon|mormon2} was carried there as a child of eleven (4 Ne. 1:8, Morm. 1:6-7). In the fourth century A.D. war broke out again in the borders of Zarahemla, by the [waters of Sidon|sidon-river] (Morm. 1:10).

place.description:
Omner was a {Nephite|nephites} city on the east borders by the seashore, named in the account of {Amalickiah|amalickiah}’s invasion around 67 BC. It was one of the cities {Amalickiah|amalickiah} captured while {Moroni|moroni1} was occupied putting down the {king-men|king-men} and regulating his own people for war; {the Lamanites|lamanites} came into [the land of Moroni|moroni], drove {the Nephites|nephites} from [the city of Moroni|moroni], and {Amalickiah|amalickiah} went on taking city after city by the seashore (Alma 51:21-27). Omner is listed in this advance alongside [Nephihah|nephihah], [Lehi|lehi], [Morianton|morianton], [Gid|gid], and [Mulek|mulek], all on the east borders by the seashore, and all strongly fortified after the manner of {Moroni|moroni1}’s own fortifications, so that they afforded strongholds for {the Lamanites|lamanites} once taken (Alma 51:26).

The east-coast region had been settled and fortified at {Moroni|moroni1}’s direction: he drove {the Lamanites|lamanites} out of [the east wilderness|east-wilderness], sent inhabitants of [Zarahemla|zarahemla] to possess the land to the borders by the seashore, and had fortifications erected along the line between {Nephite|nephites} and {Lamanite|lamanites} lands (Alma 50:7-11). In the later {Nephite|nephites} recovery, {Moroni|moroni1} and {Pahoran|pahoran1} retook [Nephihah|nephihah] and pursued {the Lamanites|lamanites} from city to city down to the borders by the seashore, where they were met by {Lehi|lehi3} and {Teancum|teancum} (Alma 62:26-32).

place.name: 모리앤툼
place.description: Moriantum was a Nephite location named in a letter from {Mormon|mormon1} to his son {Moroni|moroni2} late in Nephite history. {Mormon|mormon1} reports that the {Nephites|nephites} at Moriantum had taken many of the daughters of the {Lamanites|lamanites} prisoner and deprived them of their chastity and virtue. They then murdered the women, torturing their bodies to death, and devoured their flesh, which {Mormon|mormon1} says they did as a token of bravery. He writes that this abomination of his own people exceeded that of the {Lamanites|lamanites} (Moroni 9:9-10).
